items.titulo: How Data And Ad Tech Vendors Are Preparing For The iOS 27 Fallout
items.resumen: Against the backdrop of Advertising Week New York this week, the programmatic ecosystem has been buzzing madly like the inhabitants of an overturned beehive. That’s because Apple’s latest operating system update, iOS 27, which launched in mid-September, has been, without warning, unconditionally blocking data and identity vendors. items.titulo: YouTube to allow certified online gambling ads on Masthead from October 21
items.resumen: Posted October 7 with 14 days of lead time, the notice excludes promoters outside mandatory state or national registration. Which markets qualify is left open.

items.titulo: Ads algo discussion
items.resumen: Ads has been terrible since mid sep. Oct is way worse. Wondering if anybody has such experience before and eventually algorithms got better? If yes, how soon? submitted by /u/Unicorn1990_ [link] [comments]

items.titulo: How do I track phone calls from Google Ads in New Zealand?
items.resumen: GFN is not available, and optimising towards phone call clicks seems to be messing up my account. Are there any other options? submitted by /u/SsamAurora [link] [comments]

items.titulo: AI In Regulated Paid Media: The Default Settings That Put Compliance At Risk via @sejournal, @timothyjjensen
items.resumen: Understand how to address both ad platform and organizational AI concerns for paid media advertisers in regulated industries The post AI In Regulated Paid Media: The Default Settings That Put Compliance At Risk appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Xbox Wants What TV Has (As In, Ads); Meta’s Link Toll
items.resumen: Xbox gets into the TV biz; Meta is testing a new monetization model; and who wants to be a hold, anyway? The post Xbox Wants What TV Has (As In, Ads); Meta’s Link Toll appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Moloco gains first ad tech certification in IAB Europe retail media programme
items.resumen: ABC UK audited on-site display and sponsored product ads across web, mobile and in-app, while five more companies are under audit. What does the release omit?

items.titulo: Explaining hero image
items.resumen: A hero image is the large lead picture at the top of a page, store or ad unit, paired with a headline and button. How it loads, is specified and where it fails.

items.titulo: Explaining headline
items.resumen: Headline is the most prominent line of an ad: a text asset of about 30 characters in search that states the offer, earns the click and is combined by machine.

items.titulo: The Apple Bites Back
items.resumen: Apple has a new block list for data brokers and ad tech vendors that do cross-site user tracking – which could expand to include a much broader slate of ad tech and martech vendors across the entire ecosystem. Plus: a few thoughts on Advertising Week New York. The post The Apple Bites Back appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Raptive's Bannister links Apple's 30% App Store fee to its Safari block
items.resumen: Revised Apple Ads terms took effect July 28 while iOS 27 restricts adsrvr.org, affecting buyers and publishers. Is a 20% unblock fee coming? No source says so.

items.titulo: Nestlé Mexico Had More Scale Than It Knew What To Do With – Until It Unified Its Data
items.resumen: Prior to adopting Treasure AI, Nestlé Mexico had looked at data and targeting on a brand-by-brand basis. Now, its entire portfolio is unified in one system. The post Nestlé Mexico Had More Scale Than It Knew What To Do With – Until It Unified Its Data appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Cloudflare redesigns Radar, fed by about 20% of web traffic
items.resumen: Outages and traffic now lead Radar's landing page, with chart widgets moved behind tabs. Cloudflare gives no launch date or usage data. What else is unsaid?

items.titulo: Explaining A/B testing
items.resumen: A/B testing randomly splits an audience between two versions of an ad, page or setting and compares one metric to show which version drives the difference.

items.titulo: US households plan to cut holiday budgets 5.5%, Simon-Kucher finds
items.resumen: Homes earning $150,000-$199,999 expect $529 less than last year's forecast; 22% say discounts fully reflect true savings. Who wins without deeper markdowns?

items.titulo: 8 of 19 US podcast publishers gain downloads in Podtrac's September data
items.resumen: Meidas Media Network holds second place on the global list at 142.3 million, about 92% of it video, behind iHeart. Does video now decide who leads the tables?

items.titulo: Swedish regulator fines Miljödata SEK 1.8 million over security shortcomings
items.resumen: Intruders reached records on 2.2 million people and moved unseen for three days. Two municipalities and a region remain under review as the appeal window runs.

items.titulo: Kelly Uphoff succeeds Lauri Tarkkala as Smartly CTO
items.resumen: Nearly 10 years at Netflix and almost 5 at Tala: a new engineering chief for 800+ brands. Which start date, team size and reporting line remain undisclosed?

items.titulo: Spotify renews Joe Rogan on multi-year license, price undisclosed
items.resumen: For media buyers and publishers, a show with 18 million Spotify followers also streams on rival platforms. What the October 8 post leaves out is still open.

items.titulo: Cloudflare drops AI opt-outs from 118 sites' robots.txt, HasData finds
items.resumen: Of 592 sites declaring a GPTBot ban, 234 still served it a live page, while publishers turn away AI bots at 56.4%. Has enforcement moved from files to CDNs?

items.titulo: Beehiiv faces complaints as Lite plan rises $30 at 10,000 subscribers
items.resumen: Existing customers keep current rates until renewals on or after November 1, 2026, while Pro now reaches 250,000 subscribers. What happens to annual payers?

items.titulo: Amazon puts Google Play on Alexa tablets from $229.99
items.resumen: Pro starts at $499.99, or $549.99 with anti-glare glass; deliveries begin October 14. Alexa+ is built in, yet ads go unmentioned - will ad inventory follow?

items.titulo: Amazon puts Google Play on kids tablets from $229.99
items.resumen: Deliveries begin October 14 in four countries and October 19 in five more, with an 11-inch model at $329.99. What the release omits on children's voice data.

items.titulo: Explaining TV clearance
items.resumen: TV clearance is the review of television commercials against broadcast advertising rules before airing, run by Clearcast in Britain and network teams in the US.

items.titulo: McDonald's faces class action over menu prices at 14,000 US restaurants
items.resumen: Franchisee sales data feeds one engine, and average prices rose about 40% from 2019 to 2024, the Sherman Act complaint says. Will a court see an agreement?

items.titulo: Explaining shill
items.resumen: Shill is a person who bids, buys or praises while secretly working for the seller. How the tactic runs in auctions, reviews and ad exchanges, and the rules.

items.titulo: Explaining brigading
items.resumen: Brigading is a coordinated surge of votes, ratings, comments or reports from many online users, aimed at distorting or silencing a target such as a review page.

items.titulo: Game: Client calls expose which words you only half know
items.resumen: Sixteen terms, four groups of four. Fluency in one corner of the business will not carry you through this grid, and one group resists it entirely.

items.titulo: Game: The channel you grew up in shows in your vocabulary
items.resumen: Sixteen terms sort into four groups of four. Three sit in corners of the job plenty of buyers never work in, and the hardest group predates the web.

items.titulo: Meta's Muse accounts for 72% of AI agent requests, HUMAN finds
items.resumen: Of Muse's requests, 84% target product and search pages, and it is 25% more likely than other agents to reach checkout. Can analytics tell the traffic apart?

items.titulo: Google's spam update ends after nearly 14 days; violating sites risk demotion
items.resumen: Rollout lasted 13 days 16 hours, against 19.5 hours in March, for sites in every language. Will a core update come next? Barry Schwartz would not be surprised.

items.titulo: Google's September spam update ends after 13 days as manual actions rise
items.resumen: Google's September 2026 spam update finished on October 8 after 13 days and 16 hours, its longest run since August 2025, as SEOs report more manual actions.

items.titulo: Google Cloud adds project spend caps that pause Gemini agents at the limit
items.resumen: Per-token prices fell 98% since 2024, yet enterprise AI volume keeps straining budgets. SMBs are in early access now; wider release is promised but undated.

items.titulo: Platforms face 6-8 week wait for Google UGC Fresh Data Program answers
items.resumen: Forum and social platforms must refresh engagement counters within 72 hours and keep pages public. Google has not defined its volume and audience thresholds.

items.titulo: Explaining Search Status Dashboard
items.resumen: Search Status Dashboard is Google's public log of confirmed, widespread problems in Search crawling, indexing and serving, plus its ranking update history.

items.titulo: Explaining site reputation abuse
items.resumen: Site reputation abuse is Google's spam policy against third-party content hosted on an established website mainly to borrow its ranking strength in search.

items.titulo: SerpApi's open-source tool screens 200 Google Maps reviews for padding
items.resumen: Six pattern checks, at about 42 credits per place, test local listings for inflated star ratings. How far can an audit with stated blind spots be relied on?

items.titulo: Ecosia drops Mistral AI for open models, citing a 1-year quality gap
items.resumen: Costs roughly halved, says CEO Christian Kroll, for a search engine used by Germany's environment ministry and the NHS. Can Mistral's Large 4 model win it back?

items.titulo: Nextdoor's Halloween Treat Map gains pet and non-food treat filters
items.resumen: Reese's sponsors the U.S. edition and lists its Top 150 streets, while pins run October 8 to 31 in three countries. What does the map collect from neighbors?

items.titulo: 54% of 41 Tatari clients plan holiday TV ads before mid-November, VAB says
items.resumen: Nine panels put pixel attribution at 70% and AI use at 61% among DTC marketers, 50 days before Black Friday. Which survey details did the graphic leave out?

items.titulo: Zeta Global to add NVIDIA Nemotron-based models to AthenaOS beta in 2026
items.resumen: Early tests rate the Fireworks-tuned models on par with industry leaders, Zeta says, with no benchmark named. Where customer data is processed is not stated.

items.titulo: Zeta Global begins work on a specialized chip with an unnamed partner
items.resumen: Enterprise marketing teams can expect AthenaOS in public beta later in 2026, with general release in Q1 2027. Which technical details are still undisclosed?

items.titulo: Clear Channel puts a 15-year-old's art on nearly 2,000 digital billboards
items.resumen: Parents of 29.6 million US children want afterschool places, yet only 7 million are enrolled. Times Square carries the design October 22, but reach is unstated.

items.titulo: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on its site
items.resumen: Meta's agent became the No. 1 free app in Apple's US store within a week, then met a popup citing Amazon's usage terms. Contract claims are Amazon's open route.

items.titulo: Amazon cuts fewer than 1,000 roles on top of 30,000 since late 2025
items.resumen: Customer service, marketplace support, retail engineering, India and UK staff at Amazon got notices; leaders have scaled back planning for coming quarters.
